sup-e4cbc04ddcb4169b-q1:whole.hint: Follow what happens to the original heavy nucleus and to the particles that can trigger the next event.
notes: In fission, a heavy nucleus splits into lighter fragments, usually releasing neutrons and energy. The products have greater total binding energy.
Neutrons can enter a nucleus without electrostatic repulsion. Distinguish initiating a fission event from sustaining a chain reaction.

sup-e4cbc04ddcb4169b-q5:whole.hint: Match each reactor component to the quantity it changes: neutron speed, neutron number, or heat transfer.
notes: A moderator slows neutrons; control rods absorb neutrons; coolant removes thermal energy. These are distinct functions.
A steady chain reaction requires, on average, one subsequent fission per fission event. Critical mass depends on neutron production, absorption and escape, including the material’s geometry.

notes: Energy released is (mass_initial − mass_final)c². Equivalently, it is the increase in total binding energy, not simply the difference in binding energy per nucleon.
When given binding energy per nucleon, multiply by the nucleon number first. Keep atomic and nuclear masses consistent so electron masses cancel correctly.
